The official Supabase pricing page is the most reliable source here, and most third-party guides agree with it.

**Free plan (official docs):** Free projects get 500 MB of database size, 5 GB of egress, 5 GB of cached egress, and 1 GB of file storage. Free projects pause after one week of inactivity, and the plan allows up to 2 active projects.

**Pause behavior:** A paused project keeps its data, but the app stays offline until someone restores it from the dashboard. One guide also notes that the first request after a long pause is slow while the database wakes up.

**Pro plan (official docs):** Pro costs $25/month and includes 8 GB of disk per project, with overage at $0.125 per GB. It also includes 250 GB of egress (overage $0.09 per GB), 100 GB of file storage, and removes the inactivity pause. The Pro plan has a spend cap on by default, which you can turn off to pay for usage beyond the included quota.

**Discrepancies:** One MetaCTO table lists free egress as 2 GB, which conflicts with the official 5 GB. Another source lists free file storage as 500 MB, versus 1 GB on the official page. I'd trust the official figures. Limits can change, so verify on supabase.com/pricing before relying on them.

The official Neon sources agree on the main free-tier limits, though one docs page gives a different compute figure.

- **Compute:** Neon's FAQ and pricing page both list 100 CU-hours per project each month, and the pricing page notes that compute suspends once the monthly limit is reached Free plan quotas (100 CU-hours, 0.5 GB) are per project; compute suspends when monthly limits are reached.
- **Storage:** The cap is 0.5 GB per project. Storage is a standing limit, not a monthly one, and going over it suspends the project rather than billing you Storage, branch count, and project count are point-in-time limits: they apply continuously, not by month.
- **Other limits:** The free tier also allows 100 projects, 10 branches per project, and 5 GB of public network transfer per project per month The Neon Free plan costs $0/month and includes 100 projects, 10 branches per project, 100 CU-hours of compute per project per month, 0.5 GB of storage per project, and 5 GB of public network transfer per project per month.
- **Idle behavior:** Compute scales up to 2 CU and suspends after 5 minutes of inactivity, which cannot be disabled on Free.

Conflicting sources:
- The plans documentation gives a different figure, 50 CU-hours/project, 0.5 GB storage per branch, and 5 GB of egress. That conflicts with the 100 CU-hours in the FAQ and pricing page, and it describes storage per branch rather than per project.
- A third-party Orb blog cites 191.9 compute hours per month, which doesn't match Neon's official figures.
- Third-party pricing articles dated September 2026 repeat the 100 CU-hour and 0.5 GB figures.

The official FAQ and pricing page are the most reliable here. The 50 CU-hour figure may be an outdated docs page, so it's worth confirming on neon.com/pricing before relying on it.

content.text:
**Short version:** Neon and Supabase have real free tiers. PlanetScale's Postgres has no free tier that I could confirm. I couldn't open the vendors' pricing pages (the fetch tool was refused), so these numbers come from search-result summaries. Check them against the official pages before you rely on them.

| | Neon Free | Supabase Free | PlanetScale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Price | $0 | $0 | No free tier; cheapest paid is $5/mo |
| Storage | 0.5 GB per project | 500 MB database | n/a |
| Compute | 100 CU-hours per project per month, up to 2 CU | Not stated in what I found | n/a |
| Egress | 5 GB per project per month | 5 GB, plus 5 GB cached | n/a |
| Projects | 100 | 2 active | n/a |
| Branches | 10 per project | Not stated in what I found | n/a |
| Idle behavior | Compute suspends after 5 minutes, and this can't be turned off | Project pauses after 1 week of inactivity; you restore it manually from the dashboard | n/a |
| Other | Compute suspends when the monthly compute limit is reached | 1 GB file storage | n/a |

**Where each number comes from**
- **Neon:** The 100 CU-hours, 0.5 GB, 5 GB egress, 100 projects, 10 branches and 5-minute suspend figures come from Neon's [free plan FAQ](https://neon.com/faqs/free-plan-limits-and-quotas) and [pricing page](https://neon.com/pricing), as summarized in search results. Neon's [plans doc](https://neon.com/docs/introduction/plans) conflicts on two points. It says 50 CU-hours and 0.5 GB storage per branch, not per project. It may be outdated. A third-party article, [Jetadmin's Neon pricing guide](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/neon-pricing/), repeats the 100 CU-hour and 0.5 GB figures.
- **Supabase:** The 500 MB, 5 GB egress, 1 GB file storage, 2 active projects and 1-week pause figures come from Supabase's [pricing page](https://supabase.com/pricing.md) and [pricing docs](https://supabase.com/docs/pricing). Some third-party guides give different numbers (2 GB egress, 500 MB file storage). I went with the official figures.
- **PlanetScale:** The claim that it has no free tier, and that it removed its free Hobby plan in April 2024, comes from secondary sources: [Costbench](https://costbench.com/software/database-as-service/planetscale/), [Bytebase](https://www.bytebase.com/blog/postgres-hosting-options-pricing-comparison/) and [SolodevStack](https://solodevstack.com/blog/postgresql-vs-planetscale-solo-developers). The same sources describe a $5/mo single-node Postgres plan added October 30, 2025. One Costbench page, [PlanetScale Free Plan 2026](https://costbench.com/software/database-as-service/planetscale/free-plan/), claims a free plan, but it gives no limits and contradicts other pages on the same site, so I treated it as unreliable.

**Practical takeaway**
- **Neon:** Better for several small or experimental projects, because of the 100 projects, branching and scale-to-zero. The 0.5 GB per project cap is small.
- **Supabase:** Better if you want a bundled backend (auth, file storage). The catch is the pause after a week of inactivity and the limit of 2 active projects.
- **PlanetScale:** Budget at least $5/mo.
